named_functions.name: run_slots
named_functions.description: Runs once for slot 0 and once for slot 1, then calls update_slot. The copy that frame calls is at 01ff89f0.

named_functions.name: mix_samples
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff8f80. The byte at 0214869a is the channel count. A count of 0 returns. Otherwise each live 0x18-byte record at 02148c00 advances by its step times the sample count. Crossing the end pointer stops the channel or wraps it. 02122b0c then jumps through the list just built, ending at write_samples.

named_functions.name: write_samples
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff90fc. Shifts eight values right by 8, clamps each to the range -0x7f01 through 0x7f00, and stores them as shorts. The first four go to the buffer in r8. The next four go 0x1000 bytes later. If r8 is still below the end in r9, it jumps to the next handler.

named_functions.name: lerp_channel
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff91fc. Blends four pairs of signed bytes. The fraction in the low half of the position picks a point between a byte and the next one. The low half of the volume scales one side, and the high half scales the other. The results are added into r0 through r7, then 02122d84 jumps to the next handler.

named_functions.name: blend_bytes
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff92c8. Blends four signed bytes. The low half of the position is the step, and each sample adds that half into the high half. A carry moves the byte pointer an extra byte. The volume is in r10. 02122e34 jumps to the next handler.

named_functions.name: blend_wrap
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff9378. Blends four signed bytes the same way as lerp_channel. After each one, the step is added to the position. If that result is zero or positive, the loop length is subtracted, shifted up by 16, until the position is negative again. 02122f44 jumps to the next handler.

named_functions.name: blend_rest
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff948c. Blends signed bytes the same way as lerp_channel, but only while the position stays negative. Adding the step in r10 moves it toward zero. Once it reaches zero, the handler pointer is replaced with 02123030, and the channel is skipped from then on.

named_functions.name: blend_shorts
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff9578. Same blend as lerp_channel, but each sample is a signed short. The top of the position picks the short, and the low 16 bits blend it with the next one. Four steps are added to the position, and 021230dc jumps to the next handler.

named_functions.name: plain_bytes
named_functions.description: Runs at 01ff9784. No blend. The signed byte at the position is the whole sample, scaled by the two volume halves. The position advances by the step four times. The third loaded byte is replaced by the next address before it is scaled.

named_functions.name: start_dma
named_functions.description: Turns interrupts off, writes a DMA channel's source, destination, and control word, then restores interrupts. Runs from the ITCM copy at 01ff9998. The control word is stored last, and its top bit starts the copy.

named_functions.name: wait_vblank
named_functions.description: Waits for the next vertical blank. Thumb swi 5.

named_functions.name: startup
named_functions.description: Turns interrupts off, sets up the caches, copies the ITCM block, clears memory, and jumps to main.

named_functions.name: unpack
named_functions.description: Unpacks bytes by walking backward. startup calls it once with a null pointer, so it returns immediately. Nothing else calls it.

named_functions.name: main
named_functions.description: Turns the hardware on, initializes subsystems once, then calls frame forever.

named_functions.name: enable_screen_b
named_functions.description: Turns on the second screen's normal picture. Sets bit 0x10000 in 0x04001000 just before the frame loop.

named_functions.name: frame
named_functions.description: Runs both slots, then waits until two vertical blanks have passed.

named_functions.name: set_mode
named_functions.description: Writes the mode byte at object +0x104. Sets bit 0 of +0x106 and clears +0x105.

named_functions.name: clear_flags
named_functions.description: Clears bits in flags at object +0xc.

named_functions.name: set_flags
named_functions.description: Sets bits in flags at object +0xc.

named_functions.name: sort_point
named_functions.description: Writes the four shorts the draw sort reads. A new object stores this at +0x5c when that pointer is empty.

named_functions.name: on_screen
named_functions.description: Tests one object against the 256 by 192 screen. Overlap sets flags bit 0x1000. The selected view also sets bit 0x40000000.

named_functions.name: update_objects
named_functions.description: Walks a slot's object lists and updates each object. Draws when the second argument is 1.

named_functions.name: update_anim
named_functions.description: Steps one object's animation and writes the frame rectangle into the edge fields.

named_functions.name: update_slot
named_functions.description: Reads the slot at 027c0004 and calls update_objects with that slot's list heads.

named_functions.name: alloc_rows
named_functions.description: For each slot, reserves 0xa400 bytes at 02122300 + slot * 0x210 and splits them into 0x148 rows of 0x80 bytes. Also reserves 0x1c0 bytes for the 0x1a4 request. Then enables VRAM banks B and D and sets bit 4 of both display registers.

named_functions.name: call_run_bytes
named_functions.description: Jumps to run_bytes with the bytes at object +0x120 and +0x121. follow_link calls it when the linked animation has finished.

named_functions.name: follow_link
named_functions.description: One behavior stored at object +0x4c. Watches the mode byte and the linked object at +0x11c. When that object's animation has finished, it runs the two bytes and calls set_mode(object, 1).

named_functions.name: wobble
named_functions.description: Adds a wave to pos_b. X goes through cosine. Y goes through sine.

named_functions.name: lookup_spawn
named_functions.description: Returns the object pointer spawn saved. The first argument picks the group, and the second picks the entry.

named_functions.name: check_byte
named_functions.description: Returns 0 when run_bytes should skip a byte. A 0 byte is skipped. A 1 is skipped when bit 0 is set at 0212279c. Any other non-zero byte returns 1.

named_functions.name: run_commands
named_functions.description: Runs the byte at object +0x121 as a packed list. A word of 0 ends the list. Any other word picks a handler, then the walk steps forward by that handler's stride.

named_functions.name: spawn
named_functions.description: Creates objects for the byte at object +0x120. A 0 in an entry means that object has not been created yet. An empty +0x5c is filled with sort_point.

named_functions.name: run_bytes
named_functions.description: Reads the bytes at object +0x120 and +0x121. A byte that passes the check is used: the first goes to spawn, the second to run_commands.

named_functions.name: step_affine
named_functions.description: Steps four records of 0x6c bytes at 02122864 + 8 + slot * 0x1b8. The slot is the word at 027c0004. A record is skipped unless bits 0, 1, 2, 3, or 6 of the word at +0x18 are set. Bit 0 moves the point, bit 2 bounces a scale, bit 1 advances an angle, and bit 3 writes a rotation from cosine and sine.

named_functions.name: file_field
named_functions.description: Looks up the second argument through lookup_file. Bits 0 and 1 of the first halfword pick an address 2, 0x22, or 0x202 bytes in. That address is returned only when bits 4 and 5 are both set.

named_functions.name: blank_display
named_functions.description: Writes 0 to both display registers, 0x04000000 and 0x04001000. Writes 0x81 to VRAM bank A at 0x04000240, turning that bank on as background memory. set_display_a(1, 0, 0) stays off because the show flag is still 0.

named_functions.name: cap_step
named_functions.description: If either axis moved by 9 or more pixels, shortens the step to 8 pixels along that direction. A smaller move is kept. The length uses the hardware square root at 0x040002b8.

named_functions.name: step_point
named_functions.description: Updates one point in the current slot. Records are 0x54 bytes inside a 0x150-byte slot block. The halfword at 02122d6c selects the motion. The file value for slot 1 index 0 is 0xa010, so none of cases 0–5 run until that halfword is changed.

named_functions.name: clamp_point
named_functions.description: If the byte at record +0x4e is set, keeps the point 128 units inside the limits on the first word and 96 units inside the limits on the second. The record is 02122d24 + slot * 0x150 + index * 0x54.

named_functions.name: load_point
named_functions.description: Copies the two words at 02122d28 + index * 0x54 + slot * 0x150 into the pair the caller passed. scroll_view passes index 0, left in r1 from its own second argument.

named_functions.name: add_time
named_functions.description: Adds a 6-byte delta onto the clock at 0214112c. The fields wrap at 30, 60, 60, and 24. A wrap sets bit 0, 1, 2, or 3 of the result. The short at the start has no wrap.

named_functions.name: step_cycles
named_functions.description: Steps 12 records of 8 bytes at 0212301c + slot * 0x60. Bit 0 enables one. Byte +2 counts down, and at 0 byte +4 moves between bytes +3 and +5. A second loop of 12 records at 021231dc stops when the count passes the word at 02122fdc. That word is 0xe099900a, so the second loop returns immediately.

named_functions.name: init_palettes
named_functions.description: For slot 1, then slot 0, reserves two 0x800-byte buffers. One is paired with that screen’s background palette and one with its object palette.

named_functions.name: apply_flag
named_functions.description: Sets or clears one flag bit. The first byte picks the bit. 1 sets it through set_flags. Any other value clears it through clear_flags.

named_functions.name: cmd_set_flag
named_functions.description: Command handler 3. Looks up the object from entry bytes +4 and +5. Byte +6 picks a flag bit. Byte +7 equal to 1 sets it, and any other value clears it.

named_functions.name: cmd_set_value
named_functions.description: Command handler 2. Looks up the object from entry bytes +4 and +5, stores the short at entry +6 into object +0x14, and sets bit 0x8 on the byte at +0x106. A negative short becomes 0.

named_functions.name: cmd_set_mode
named_functions.description: Command handler 1. Looks up the object from entry bytes +4 and +5, calls set_mode(object, 1), and sets flags bit 0x8. The entry is 8 bytes.

named_functions.name: set_callbacks
named_functions.description: Stores 01ff8c50 at 02123498 and 01ff82b4 at 0212349c. Both addresses are functions in the ITCM copy. Other functions load those two words and call them.

named_functions.name: tick_delays
named_functions.description: Returns while the count at 021234a4 is 0. Otherwise counts down byte +2 of each 8-byte record at 021234a8. A byte that reaches 0 calls 0203241c with that record, unless bit 0 of byte +3 is set.

named_functions.name: load_file
named_functions.description: Loads one file from rom.bin.

named_functions.name: lookup_file
named_functions.description: Returns the pointer already stored for a file. An id of 0x344A or higher is already a pointer and is returned unchanged.

named_functions.name: age_files
named_functions.description: Walks 0x344a file slots. A loaded file whose byte at 0213d77c has bit 7 clear counts down the low 7 bits. At 0, the pointer at 02130654 is cleared. run_slots calls it with 0.

named_functions.name: init_fs
named_functions.description: Sets up the filesystem for the device named rom. main calls it once, with interrupts on, before the boot files are loaded.

named_functions.name: copy_blocks
named_functions.description: Copies blocks of words for the current slot. The block size is the word at slot-block +0x24. It does not read the 32-piece list.

named_functions.name: load_boot_file
named_functions.description: Loads one of the eight boot files and copies its header into the 0x14-byte record at 02140d60.

named_functions.name: attach_file
named_functions.description: Attaches one loaded boot file to the current slot. The slot word is 027c0004. The 0x3c-byte block starts at 02140ce8.

named_functions.name: load_boot_files
named_functions.description: Calls load_boot_file for indexes 0 through 7, then clears the slot blocks at 02140ce8.

named_functions.name: alloc_extra
named_functions.description: Calls five setup functions. One returns immediately. The others reserve a 0x400-byte block, an 0x8c00-byte block, and two 0xc80-byte row lists.

named_functions.name: record_active
named_functions.description: Returns 0 only when the word at 02141c70 + index * 0x40 is 0 and the short at 02141c80 + index * 0x40 is 0. Any other case returns 1.

named_functions.name: mark_record
named_functions.description: On the record selected by the halfword at 02141d74, ORs 3 into the word at +4. If the short at +0x12 differs from a 0-to-43 level, it refreshes that short first.

named_functions.name: update_record
named_functions.description: Handles one 0x40-byte record at 02141c70. The flag word at 02141c74 gates the branches. A zero flag word skips them. update_list calls it with index 0.

named_functions.name: read_input
named_functions.description: On slot 0, reads the buttons from 0x04000130 and the halfword at 027fffa8. Stores held, previous, pressed, and released at 02141dc6. A nonzero byte at 02141d70 skips that and clears the block instead.

named_functions.name: mark_block
named_functions.description: Clears the byte at 02141d70 and a run of halfwords in that block, then stores the halfword 1 at 02141d72.

named_functions.name: start_vblank
named_functions.description: Replaces the V-Blank handler with 01ff86fc, sets IE bit 0 and DISPSTAT bit 3, turns the master interrupt switch on, and stores 0203b344 at 027c0028.

named_functions.name: set_frame_counter
named_functions.description: Stores 027c0028 at 027c0020. frame reads the counter through that pointer, so the new count is at 027c0044 and the accepted count is at 027c0048.

named_functions.name: show_label
named_functions.description: Shows one label, picked by the argument. Cases 0–4 run when the word at 027c0084 + slot * 0x8c is 0. Cases 5 and 10–18 run only when that word is 8. The two bytes at 020c77b4 + index * 2 are the position. 020a6d28 looks up the text in the 0x400-byte block at 02148f74.

named_functions.name: id_matches
named_functions.description: Returns 1 when the id byte equals one of three bytes in the 8-byte record at 020c812c, or one of 11 bytes at 020c8110. The record is selected by the first byte of the block passed in.

named_functions.name: update_list
named_functions.description: Entry 1 of the table call_entry uses. Walks the count at 02141d72, which mark_block set to 1, and updates the 0x40-byte records at 02141c70.

named_functions.name: clamp_positive
named_functions.description: Turns a negative short into 0 and keeps a positive short. cmd_set_value uses it on the short at entry +6 before storing it at object +0x14.

named_functions.name: cosine
named_functions.description: Adds 0x40 to the angle index and jumps to sine. That is one quarter turn.

named_functions.name: sine
named_functions.description: Looks up one quarter of a 256-step circle. The peak value is 0x10000, one pixel.

named_functions.name: call_entry
named_functions.description: Calls the function at 020cd8b8 + index * 0xc, where the index is the first word of the slot record at 027c0070. A 0 pointer returns. The table has 43 entries. Entry 0 returns immediately. Entry 1 is update_list.

named_functions.name: call_mode
named_functions.description: Calls the function at 020cd8b4 + index * 0xc. The index is the first word of the slot record at 027c0070. A 0 pointer returns. Slot 0’s index is 0, and that entry is bx lr.

named_functions.name: record_changed
named_functions.description: Returns 1 when the word at 027c0070 + slot * 0x8c differs from the word 0x2c bytes later. init_slots copied those words, so they start equal and this returns 0.

named_functions.name: init_slots
named_functions.description: Clears the two 0x8c-byte records at 027c0070 and 027c00fc. Copies the first 11 words into the two groups at +0x2c and +0x58, then writes 0x83 at +0x2c. Slot 0 also reserves 0x800 bytes.

named_functions.name: zero_memory
named_functions.description: Writes zeros through a range of bytes. load_boot_files uses it to clear 0x3c bytes at each slot block.

named_functions.name: take_main_memory
named_functions.description: Reads arena 0, the free main RAM from 0214de20 to 023c0000. Rounds the ends to multiples of 32, which they already are, then saves that range and adds 1 to the count at 02142000.

named_functions.name: clear_state
named_functions.description: Stores 0 at 02142100, 0214210c, and 02142110. A nearby function sets those same words to 1.

named_functions.name: do_nothing_3
named_functions.description: Returns immediately. The bytes are 1e ff 2f e1. alloc_extra calls it.

named_functions.name: tick_events
named_functions.description: Returns while the byte at 02142234 is 0. Otherwise ticks ten 6-byte timers at 02142270 and counts down the word at 02142238. The scan of ids 0x1f through 0x50 runs only on the call where that word was already 0, then stores 0x96.

named_functions.name: hide_sprites
named_functions.description: From the byte at 021435d5 + slot * 0x132c through index 127, sets bits 8 and 9 of each 8-byte entry to the hidden value 0x200. It does that in both banks, 0x400 bytes apart, inside the slot block at 021422ac. Then stores 1 at 027c0060 + slot.

named_functions.name: init_slot_blocks
named_functions.description: Builds a 0x132c-byte record per slot at 021422ac. The first word points 8 bytes into the record. Slot 0’s next word points at 02142ab4. The helpers run once with the slot at 1 and once at 0.

named_functions.name: clear_link
named_functions.description: Clears bit 0 of the object's flags, then stores 0 at +0x120 and +0x11c. find_target calls it with the word at 02144938 when the mode byte is not 0x10.

named_functions.name: walk_links
named_functions.description: Returns while the halfword at 02144b80 + slot * 0x150 is 0. Otherwise walks the list at +4 of that record. Bit 15 of the word at record +0x30 skips 0206e440, and that bit is then cleared.

named_functions.name: alloc_slot_rows
named_functions.description: For each slot, at 02144a48 + slot * 0x150, reserves 0x54 rows of 0x14 bytes and 0x48 rows of 5 bytes, plus four 0x60-byte blocks. Clears the words at +0 and +4.

named_functions.name: init_node
named_functions.description: Points 02144ce8 at 02144d44 and fills that record: 0, 1, 0, -1, and the halfword 0xffff at +0x10. Also points 02144cec at 02144d30.

named_functions.name: seed_block
named_functions.description: Asks channel 5 to fill stack values, packs them into one word at 02146f08, adds 1 to 02146f0c, and writes that word into the block at 02146ef8.

named_functions.name: alloc_block
named_functions.description: Asks the main-memory range for 0x9c4 bytes. The allocator rounds that up to 0x9e0 and stores the pointer at 02146ef8.

named_functions.name: step_tasks
named_functions.description: If the byte at 02146f18 is 0, returns. Otherwise walks the three 0xa0-byte records at 02146f1c. State bytes 0 and 1 clear a record. State 2 or 3 calls the function at 020f7254 + index * 8.

named_functions.name: init_header
named_functions.description: Reserves 0xfe0 bytes and stores the pointer at 0214711c. On a zeroed header, copies URBZ0010 from 020f7328 to 021470fc, clears the block, and passes (0x20, 0x40) and (0x1000, 0x40) with that pointer.

named_functions.name: slot_pending
named_functions.description: Returns 1 when the word at 02147194 + slot * 0x20 is not 0. init_fade stored 0 there, so run_slots skips the next block. The slot is the word at 027c0004.

named_functions.name: flag_slot
named_functions.description: ORs 0x4000 shifted by the slot into 027c0008, and ORs 5 into the word at 02147194 + slot * 0x20. That is the word slot_pending tests.

named_functions.name: set_fade
named_functions.description: Stores the second argument in the current slot’s record at 0214719c + slot * 0x20, then calls 02080584. Command 0x3f writes the master brightness. main uses slot 1, then slot 0, both with 0x10, writing 0x4010 to 0x0400106c and 0x0400006c.

named_functions.name: init_fade
named_functions.description: Writes 1, 0, and 0x3f at 02147190 and again at 021471b0. Those are the two slot records. set_fade stored 0x10 just after each group, at 0214719c and 021471bc.

named_functions.name: load_map_size
named_functions.description: Copies the two words at 021472a0 + slot * 0x114 into the pair the caller passes. That is 0xd0 bytes into the same slot record scroll_view uses. The first word is the width and the second is the height.

named_functions.name: cache_tile
named_functions.description: Finds a tile in the layer cache, or copies its 32 bytes into background memory and returns the new index. A tile already cached has its count increased instead.

named_functions.name: write_row
named_functions.description: Wraps an X into the map width, then writes 33 background-map entries across the strip through cache_tile. The step is 8 pixels. Slot 0 uses 0x06000000 and slot 1 uses 0x06200000.

named_functions.name: write_column
named_functions.description: Wraps an X into the map width, then writes 25 background-map entries down the strip. Slot 0 uses 0x06000000 and slot 1 uses 0x06200000.

named_functions.name: load_row
named_functions.description: Uses the same wrap as load_column, then releases 33 cached tiles across the strip for each enabled layer. The step between tiles is 8 pixels.

named_functions.name: load_column
named_functions.description: Wraps an X into the map width, then releases 25 cached tiles down the strip for each enabled layer. A width of 0 never leaves the wrap, because subtracting 0 leaves the position at 0.

named_functions.name: release_tile
named_functions.description: Looks up a tile in the layer's chain at 021472b0. A missing tile returns 1. A found tile loses one from its count, and a count of 0 unhooks that 6-byte record.

named_functions.name: flush_scroll
named_functions.description: For two pairs at record +0x30 and +0x38, a value other than -1 is passed to load_column or load_row, and then both words are set to -1. Then the view at 021471f0 is copied to 021471f8.

named_functions.name: queue_scroll
named_functions.description: Stores the two arguments at 02147200 + slot * 0x114 + which * 8. Those are the pairs flush_scroll later reads at record +0x30 and +0x38. which is 0 or 1.

named_functions.name: scroll_view
named_functions.description: Turns the current point into the top-left of a 256 by 192 view and keeps that view inside the map. A change of 8 pixels loads the new row or column. update_list calls it as scroll_view(0, 0).

named_functions.name: do_nothing_4
named_functions.description: Returns immediately. The bytes are 1e ff 2f e1, which is bx lr.

named_functions.name: adjust_level
named_functions.description: Compares a new level with the top byte of the word at 02141220. A higher new level calls 0205dc20 with 0x27. A lower one calls it with 0x29. An equal level returns.

named_functions.name: step_state
named_functions.description: Asks add_time about the 6-byte entry. If bits 1–3 of the result are clear, it returns. Otherwise it sets bits 0 and 1 on the current 0x40-byte record and steps the block at 02141120.

named_functions.name: set_delta
named_functions.description: Stores one byte at 021473f8. That byte picks the 6-byte clock delta at 02113b5c. find_target reads it, then calls this with 0.

named_functions.name: find_target
named_functions.description: Clears 021473fc, then looks at the object pointer in 02141c2c. Mode 0x10 at object +0x104 searches the list at 0214490c and may store that object's +0x24 into 021473fc. A newly pressed B button calls through the pointer at object +0x100.

named_functions.name: scan_channels
named_functions.description: Reads the count byte at 0214869a. From count minus 1 down to 0, an index whose bit is clear in the word at 021488f4 is passed to update_channel with 0. A count of 0 returns immediately.

named_functions.name: update_channel
named_functions.description: One channel. The 0x18-byte record is at 02148c00 + index * 0x18, and the link byte is at 021479cc + index * 0x20 + 10. A second argument of 0 calls mix_channel with the index and stores 0xff in that link byte. 0xff as the index returns immediately.

named_functions.name: set_scale
named_functions.description: Clamps the argument to 0x20 through 0xff and stores it at 02147520 + 0x21. Two fifths of that value, rounded down, divides the word at 02148680 shifted left 8. The hardware divider is 0204d964. The quotient, shifted left 8, is stored at 02148684 and 02148688.

named_functions.name: free_copy
named_functions.description: Frees the block flush_block copies to 02147520. Byte +0x1c being 1 or 2 calls scan_channels and clears it. Bit 7 of byte +0x23 is the release. Bit 1 of byte +0x1d chooses a full free, ending in reset_buffer, or just storing 0 at 0214751c. The block starts cleared, and flush_block does not call this on the first frame.

named_functions.name: apply_copy
named_functions.description: Runs when byte +0x1c of the block at 02147520 is 2. Copies 0x18-byte records from 02148900 into 02148c00 for each index whose bit is clear in the word at 021488f4. A set bit stores 0xff into the link byte instead. Then stores 1 at byte +0x1c.

named_functions.name: flush_block
named_functions.description: Tests the word at 0214868c. Bit 5 copies 0x8ac bytes from 02147dcc to 02147520, clears three source bytes, and then clears the bit. Bit 4 only calls free_copy and clears itself. Both bits are clear on the first frame, so it returns.

named_functions.name: add_count
named_functions.description: If bit 2 of the word at 0214868c is clear, adds 0x100 to the halfword at 02148694. That halfword is the sample count pump_audio consumes. A set bit returns without adding.

named_functions.name: apply_mix
named_functions.description: Adds the shorts at 02148690 and 02148692 into the two buffer halves, clamped to -0x8000 through 0x7fff. Each sample then shrinks those shorts by (count - 1) / count. The empty loop waits on divider bit 15 at 0x04000280. The shorts are cleared at the end.

named_functions.name: mix_channel
named_functions.description: If the channel's first word is set, multiplies one sample by the halfwords at +0xc and +0xe, shifts each product right 9, and adds them to the shorts at 02148690 and 02148692. Then stores 0 in the channel word. A zero word returns.

named_functions.name: set_rate
named_functions.description: If the argument differs from the halfword at 02148698, stores it there. Divides 0xffb0ff by that value, rounds the quotient to a multiple of 32 at 02148696, and divides 0xffb0ff by the rounded value into 02148680. Then calls set_scale. A new value while bit 2 of 0214868c is clear also calls mark_once and reset_buffer.

named_functions.name: pick_table
named_functions.description: Bit 0 of the argument picks a 0x30-byte table. Clear copies 020b42a4 onto 020b4274. Set copies 020b42d4, which already matches those bytes. The whole argument is then stored at 0214868c.

named_functions.name: pump_audio
named_functions.description: Reads the flag word at 0214868c. Bit 2 set and bit 3 clear returns. Bit 3 set clears the halfword at 02148694 and bit 7 of byte +0x1c at 02147520, then starts eight channels through send_channel, calls queue_reply and queue_nine(0xff, 0, 1, 0), and clears bits 2 and 3. Both bits clear consumes that halfword as a sample count.

named_functions.name: free_channels
named_functions.description: Walks 16 records of 0x20 bytes from 02148880 down to 021486a0. A record whose first word is set is freed through 0204e4b4 when its countdown hits 0, or when bit 7 of byte +0xe is clear and the 0x18-byte record at 02148c00 is empty. clear_area zeroed this block, so the first call frees nothing.

named_functions.name: reset_buffer
named_functions.description: If bit 2 of 0214868c is clear, returns. Otherwise clears 0x2000 bytes at the pointer in 0214867c, divides the word at 02148680 by 0x3c0ded on the hardware divider, stores a scaled halfword at 02148694, copies the pointer to 02148678, clears 02148690, and sets bit 3 of 0214868c.

named_functions.name: mark_once
named_functions.description: If bit 2 of 0214868c is clear, adds 1 to the byte at 0214cd88, sets that bit, and sets bit 7 of the byte at 0214753c. Later calls return immediately.

named_functions.name: clear_area
named_functions.description: Clears 0x260 bytes at 021486a0, then stores the byte 0x20 at 021488fa. FUN_02098488 then clears 0x28 bytes at 02148678 and 0xc00 bytes at 02148c00.

named_functions.name: reserve_block
named_functions.description: Looks up file 0x37 from the table at 0211be40, stores the byte 0x2e at 02148f70, then asks the main-memory range for 0x400 bytes and stores that pointer at 02148f74.

named_functions.name: clear_entry
named_functions.description: For one index, stores the pointer 02148fec at 02148fe8 + index * 16, stores 0 at 02148fec + index * 16 and 02148ff4 + index * 16, and clears bit 0 of the byte at offset 8.

named_functions.name: init_four
named_functions.description: Calls clear_entry with 0, 1, 2, and 3. The early return Ghidra marked unreachable is the check before the first pass, and the counter starts at 0.

named_functions.name: clear_slot_buffers
named_functions.description: Saves the slot, then for slot 0 and slot 1 clears 0x400 bytes at 02149864 + slot * 0x400 and fills 0x400 bytes at 02149064 + slot * 0x400 with 0xff. Restores the slot afterward.

named_functions.name: step_motions
named_functions.description: Two records of 0x3c bytes at 0214a064 + slot * 0x78. Each holds two motions. Bit 1 of a motion moves its point: a countdown of 0 adds the step, 1 snaps to the target and clears the bit, and any other value steps toward the target. The base is past arm9.bin and starts cleared, so all four motions are skipped.

named_functions.name: blend_up
named_functions.description: Same four byte blends as blend_wrap. After each step, a negative position subtracts the loop length shifted up by 16 until the position is zero or positive. blend_wrap does that subtract while the position is zero or positive.

named_functions.name: rest_bytes
named_functions.description: A byte-for-byte copy of blend_rest. The scratch word is the one at 020b4414, and the skip stub is at 020b44fc. Same blend, and the handler is replaced once the position reaches zero.

named_functions.name: next_node
named_functions.description: A second argument of 0 returns the header's first word, the head. Otherwise it returns the next word at node + offset + 4. The offset is the halfword at header +10.

named_functions.name: unlink_record
named_functions.description: Removes a record from the doubly linked list whose header is the first argument. The halfword at header +10 is the offset of the previous and next words. The halfword at header +8 is the count, and it drops by 1.

named_functions.name: link_node
named_functions.description: Appends the node at the tail. Its previous word becomes the old tail and its next word becomes 0. The header's second word moves to the new node, and the count at header +8 increases by 1. An empty list calls first_node instead.

named_functions.name: first_node
named_functions.description: Stores 0 in both of the node's link words. The header's first and second words both become this node, and the count at header +8 increases by 1.

named_functions.name: flush_pending
named_functions.description: Calls reclaim_list(0) until it returns 0, then calls step_nodes, step_span, and step_four. file_queue(0) tries to send the queue once and does not wait.

named_functions.name: init_records
named_functions.description: Runs once. Clears three words at 0214a18c and two words at 0214a9fc and 0214aa14. Builds 32 records of 0x1c bytes at 0214a1b0, then 16 records of 0x44 bytes at 0214a530. The first of those 16 is linked from 0214a198.

named_functions.name: clear_mask
named_functions.description: Clears bit 1 << index in the word at 0214a190. The shift uses the low 8 bits of the index. init_records cleared that word, so it starts at 0.

named_functions.name: clear_held
named_functions.description: Clears the argument's bits in the word at 0214a18c. close_span passes the word at +0x24. No command is filed.

named_functions.name: clear_bits
named_functions.description: Calls queue_23 with the mask and 0. Then clears those bits in the word at 0214a194. A mask of 0 returns.

named_functions.name: retire_node
named_functions.description: Clears the node's first word through the pointer it holds, unlinks the node from the list stored at +4, and moves the pointer at +8 onto the list 12 bytes after that header. Then moves the node itself from 0214a1a4 onto 0214a198 and stores 0 in byte +0x2c.

named_functions.name: finish_node
named_functions.description: Passes the byte at +0x3c to queue_one, then calls retire_node. step_nodes does this when byte +0x2c is 2 and count_done returns 1.

named_functions.name: step_nodes
named_functions.description: Walks the list at 0214a1a4. When count_reached accepts the word at +0x30, byte +0x2d becomes 1. A set byte whose bit is clear in the mask from second_word calls retire_node. Otherwise raise_count runs on the block at +0x1c. The third table index is slide_value on that block, shifted right by 8. Three signed halfwords from 0211c850 are added, and a new sum is passed to report_sum. Byte +0x2c equal to 2 and count_done on that block calls finish_node.

named_functions.name: release_record
named_functions.description: Passes the word at +0x28 to clear_mask, then calls unlink_record with 0214a970 and the record. Clears bits 0 and 1 of the word at +0xc.

named_functions.name: clear_bit
named_functions.description: If bit 1 of the word at +0xc is set, passes the same four values as queue_bit to queue_ten, clears that bit, saves read_count, and calls file_queue(1). The saved value is then passed to wait_count. release_record runs either way.

named_functions.name: spread_sum
named_functions.description: Stores the new sum at +0x24. If the count at +0x30 is 0 or negative, returns. Otherwise each byte at +0x34 picks an 8-byte entry at 0214a97c, and queue_17 is called with 1 shifted by that byte and the two halves of pack_level's result.

named_functions.name: pass_record
named_functions.description: If bit 0 of the word at +0xc is set, calls clear_bit with the record still in r0. A clear bit returns.

named_functions.name: queue_bit
named_functions.description: Queues command 9. The first word is the word at record +0x2c. The third word is 1 shifted by the low 8 bits of the word at +0x28. Then sets bit 1 of the word at +0xc. step_four passes each of the four records at 0214aa7c.

named_functions.name: clear_source
named_functions.description: If the word at +0x2c is not 0, calls clear_bits with that word still in r0, then stores 0 at +0x2c and +0x30.

named_functions.name: close_span
named_functions.description: Shuts down the record at 0214aa14 and stores 0 in its first word. queue_ten gets the words at +0x20 and +0x24, and a nonzero +0x24 is also passed to clear_held. A word at +0x28 of 0 or more also sends 1 shifted by that word's low 8 bits, then waits out file_queue(1), calls take_one on 0214aa00 until it returns 0, and calls clear_mask with that word. A nonzero word at +0x1c is passed to clear_bits. If the word at +4 is 1, queue_21 is called with four zeros.

named_functions.name: step_span
named_functions.description: One record at 0214aa14. A zero first word returns, and a nonzero word at +4 returns. Otherwise raise_count runs on the block at +0x38. A nonzero word at +0x48 with count_done calls close_span. Otherwise slide_value shifted right by 8 is compared with the word at +0x4c, and a change calls queue_17 with the word at +0x20.

named_functions.name: pass_node
named_functions.description: With interrupts off, calls link_node with the header at 0214aa64 and the node. That header is the 12 bytes just before the list at 0214aa70.

named_functions.name: lower_count
named_functions.description: If the word at +0x100 is 0, returns. Otherwise subtracts 1. When that reaches 0, calls clear_source with the record still in r0.

named_functions.name: finish_record
named_functions.description: Clears the pointer at +0x114 and the word it points at, then calls lower_count. Bit 4 of the word at +0x50 calls reset_block on record + 0x44. Walks the list at 0214aa70 with next_node and unlinks every node whose word at +8 is this record, then calls pass_node on that node. Clears bits 0, 1, and 2 of the word at +0xf0.

named_functions.name: close_record
named_functions.description: If bit 1 of the word at +0xf0 is set, calls pass_record with the record still in r0. Then always calls finish_record with the record.

named_functions.name: step_four
named_functions.description: Walks four records of 0x12c bytes from 0214aa7c. Bit 0 of the word at +0xf0 has to be set. A nonzero word at +0xf4 calls close_record and skips the rest. Bit 2 with a nonzero word at +0xf8 calls queue_bit, then sets bit 1 and clears bit 2. Bit 1 adds two signed halfwords from 0211c850. A changed sum is passed to spread_sum. Bit 3 with count_done on the block at +0xc8 calls close_record.

named_functions.name: count_done
named_functions.description: Returns 1 when the signed word at +8 has reached the signed word at +0xc. Otherwise returns 0.

named_functions.name: raise_count
named_functions.description: If the signed word at +8 is still below the signed word at +0xc, adds 1 to the word at +8. step_nodes passes node + 0x1c.

named_functions.name: slide_value
named_functions.description: While the signed word at +8 is below the word at +0xc, returns the word at +0 plus (+8) * ((+4) - (+0)) divided by the word at +0xc through divide_signed. Once +8 has reached +0xc, returns the word at +4.

named_functions.name: do_nothing
named_functions.description: Returns immediately. main calls it just before FUN_020b5ffc.

named_functions.name: set_display_a
named_functions.description: Writes the first screen's display register. Saves the mode ushort at 0214af2c. If the flag at 0212195c is 0, the mode is forced to 0.

named_functions.name: show_display_a
named_functions.description: Puts the saved mode back on the first screen. A saved 0 becomes mode 1, the normal picture. Sets the flag at 0212195c to 1.

named_functions.name: hide_display_a
named_functions.description: Saves bits 16 and 17 of the first screen into 0214af2c, clears the flag at 0212195c, and clears those two bits so the picture is off.

named_functions.name: reset_display
named_functions.description: Turns the screens on, disables VRAM, clears both display register blocks, and sets background 2 and 3 on each screen back to normal size.

named_functions.name: disable_vram
named_functions.description: Disables every VRAM bank by writing 0 to 0x04000240–0x04000246 and 0x04000248. Also clears 13 ushorts at 0214af30.

named_functions.name: allow_interrupts
named_functions.description: Turns the master switch 0x04000208 off, ORs the argument into the enable mask 0x04000210, restores the switch, and returns the old mask. main calls it with 1, then with 0x40000.

named_functions.name: set_irq_handler
named_functions.description: For each set bit in the mask, stores a handler. Bits 0–2, 7, and 12–21 write one word in the table at 02121974. Bits 3–6 and 8–11 write a 12-byte record at 0214af4c: the handler, then 1, then 0. main passes mask 1 and 02000c94, so only the V-Blank slot changes.

named_functions.name: clear_flag
named_functions.description: Stores the halfword 0 at 027c0188, which is 0x188 bytes into the block copied to 027c0000. Later code treats a nonzero value there as a one-shot.

named_functions.name: init_lock
named_functions.description: Runs once. Takes id 0x7e on the word at 027ffff0, waits until the halfword at 027ffff6 is 0, fills the small table at 027fffb0, gives both cartridge slots to the ARM7, releases 0x7e, and takes id 0x7f.

named_functions.name: halt
named_functions.description: Turns interrupts on, then waits for an interrupt forever. fill_heap_head stores 020b6ff0, the instruction after the register save.

named_functions.name: set_heap_word
named_functions.description: With interrupts off, replaces the word at heap header +0x10 and returns the old word. init_heap passes 0.

named_functions.name: switch_heap
named_functions.description: If the CPU is in interrupt mode, or a ushort flag is set, stores 1 and returns. Otherwise compares two heap records and may switch.

named_functions.name: find_marked_heap
named_functions.description: Walks the heap list at header +0xc and returns the first heap whose +0x64 is 1. Returns 0 when none is marked.

named_functions.name: mark_heaps
named_functions.description: Loads the halfword at the pointer it is given and uses that as the mask. For each heap whose slot bit is set, +0x64 is set to 1. Then the mask is cleared.

named_functions.name: yield_heap
named_functions.description: With interrupts off, ORs 1 << slot into the halfword argument when it is not 0. The slot is the low 8 bits of the word at +0x6c of the heap record reached through 0214afb4. Stores 0 at that record's +0x64, then calls switch_heap.

named_functions.name: release_heap
named_functions.description: Turns interrupts off, loads the heap record through header +8, clears that heap's slot, and sets +0x64 to 2.

named_functions.name: add_heap
named_functions.description: With interrupts off, picks a slot, writes the two end markers, and clears the bytes between them. init_heap uses it for a 0xc8-byte range ending at 0214b200.

named_functions.name: init_heap
named_functions.description: Runs once. Records the free range 027c01a0–027c37c0 and writes a marker at each end.

named_functions.name: insert_heap
named_functions.description: Links a heap into the list at header +0xc. The next heap is +0x68. Smaller +0x70 values come first.

named_functions.name: find_heap_slot
named_functions.description: Returns the index of the first zero word in the 16 slots at heap header +0x14. Returns -1 when all 16 are full.

named_functions.name: fill_heap_head
named_functions.description: Fills the front of a heap record. Stores 0x1f when the code pointer is even and 0x3f when it is odd. Zeros the words from +4 through +0x34, and the word at +0x3c.

named_functions.name: save_context
named_functions.description: Saves the CPU state into the heap record and returns 0, so switch_heap takes the normal switch path. Calls save_divider with the record plus 0x48 first. That copies the divider numerator from 0x04000290, the denominator from 0x04000298, the square-root input from 0x040002b8, and the mode bits from 0x04000280 and 0x040002b0.

named_functions.name: restore_context
named_functions.description: Calls restore_divider with the record plus 0x48, loads the saved registers, and resumes with subs pc, lr, #4. That instruction is the jumptable warning.

named_functions.name: return_zero
named_functions.description: Returns 0. main would store 1 vblank if this returned anything else, so frame keeps waiting for two.

named_functions.name: take_one
named_functions.description: If the word at +0x10 is 0 and bit 0 of the third argument is set, calls yield_heap with block + 2 until the count is nonzero. Otherwise returns 0. A nonzero count stores the word at base[index] through the second argument when that pointer is set, sets the index at +0xc to the remainder of (index + 1) / word at +8, subtracts 1 from the count, and calls mark_heaps with the block. Returns 1.

named_functions.name: pop_heap_node
named_functions.description: Removes the first node in the list at heap record +0x7c and returns it. The next node is at the node's +0x10. +0x80 is cleared when the list becomes empty.

named_functions.name: drain_heap
named_functions.description: If the word at +0x7c is 0, returns. Otherwise takes items from pop_heap_node until that word is 0.

named_functions.name: invalidate_lines
named_functions.description: Drops one 32-byte data-cache line at a time from the aligned start through start + length. fresh_word passes the shared block and 0x280.

named_functions.name: clean_lines
named_functions.description: Writes each dirty 32-byte data-cache line back to main memory, then drops it. file_queue passes the command records at 0214b580 and 0x1800.

named_functions.name: init_subsystems
named_functions.description: Calls the IPC handshake, init_heap, and several other setup functions. main calls init_heap again afterward, and that second call returns immediately.

named_functions.name: do_nothing_2
named_functions.description: Returns immediately. init_subsystems calls it. The bytes are 1e ff 2f e1, which is bx lr.

named_functions.name: init_arenas
named_functions.description: Runs once. Writes the low and high address of seven memory areas into tables at 027fe23c and 027fe260.

named_functions.name: init_irq
named_functions.description: Installs 020b7fc0 as the ARM9 interrupt handler at 027ffd9c and 027c3fdc, unless a handler in 02600000–027fffff is already saved and bit 30 of the check word is set.

named_functions.name: clear_vcount
named_functions.description: Runs once. Clears the two words at 0214b294, then clears bit 2 of 0x04000210 while 0x04000208 is off. Bit 2 is the V-Counter interrupt.

named_functions.name: enable_irq
named_functions.description: Clears the interrupt-disable bit and returns the old flag.

named_functions.name: disable_irq
named_functions.description: Reads the interrupt flag, turns interrupts off, and returns the old flag.

named_functions.name: restore_irq
named_functions.description: Writes that saved flag back.

named_functions.name: wait_irq
named_functions.description: Puts the CPU to sleep until the next interrupt. mov r0, #0, then the coprocessor wait.

named_functions.name: busy_wait
named_functions.description: Subtracts 4 and repeats while the value before that subtract was at least 4. wait_channel passes 100.

named_functions.name: on_channel_12
named_functions.description: Handler for channel 12. If bits 8–14 of the message are 0x10, stores the halfword 1 at 0214b2a0. Any other value does not return.

named_functions.name: init_channel_12
named_functions.description: Runs once. Waits until bit 12 is set at 027fff8c, then stores on_channel_12 at 0214ce18 and sets bit 12 at 027fff88.

named_functions.name: set_wram
named_functions.description: Stores one byte at 0x04000247. init_subsystems passes 3, which gives all 32KB of shared WRAM to the ARM7.

named_functions.name: dma_fill
named_functions.description: Fills a range through DMA channel param_1. Boot uses channel 3 to fill display registers with 0. Waits while bit 31 of the channel control word is set.

named_functions.name: fill_words
named_functions.description: Writes one value, as a word, from a start address through a byte count. add_heap uses it to store 0 between the two markers.

named_functions.name: copy_bytes
named_functions.description: Copies the third argument's number of bytes from the first pointer to the second. A count of 0 returns. Even addresses are copied 4 bytes at a time. An odd destination copies one byte first. build_path uses it for the leading bytes, :/, and each name.

named_functions.name: init_channel_7
named_functions.description: Runs once. The word at 0214b2a4 stops a second call. Calls init_queue, then 020b93e4.

named_functions.name: queue_command
named_functions.description: Asks take_record for a record. A 0 return leaves. Otherwise the five arguments are stored at +4 through +0x14. link_record then links that record: 0214b2b0 stays at the first one, and 0214b2b4 moves to the newest.

named_functions.name: queue_three
named_functions.description: Calls queue_command(3, first, second, third, fourth). report_sum passes the node's byte, 6, the new sum, and 2.

named_functions.name: queue_21
named_functions.description: Calls queue_command(0x15, first, second, third, fourth). close_span passes four zeros when the word at +4 is 1.

named_functions.name: send_channel
named_functions.description: Packs a command numbered 11 and passes it to 020b8964. For pump_audio, the channel is in the low half of the next word and the halfword at 02148696 is in the high half. The pointer is the word after that. The other two packed words are 0x7f000400 and 0x01000000.

named_functions.name: queue_17
named_functions.description: Calls queue_command(0x11, first, second, third, 0). step_span passes the word at +0x20, the shifted slide value, and 0.

named_functions.name: queue_23
named_functions.description: Calls queue_command(0x17, first, second, 0, 0). clear_bits passes the mask and 0, so the command words are 0x17, the mask, and three zeros.

named_functions.name: queue_reply
named_functions.description: Calls set_reply with the first, fourth, and fifth arguments, then queue_command(0xf, first, second, third, new tag). pump_audio passes index 0, function add_count, argument 0, and the halfword at 02148696 shifted left by 3.

named_functions.name: queue_ten
named_functions.description: For each set bit in the low 8 bits of the third argument, calls bump_tag with that bit's index. Then calls queue_command(10, first, second, third, fourth).

named_functions.name: queue_nine
named_functions.description: Passes 9 and then its four arguments to queue_command. pump_audio calls it as (0xff, 0, 1, 0).

named_functions.name: report_sum
named_functions.description: Tail-calls queue_three with the node's byte, 6, the new sum, and 2. The branch at 020b8c84 is that jump. step_nodes calls it when the stored halfword at +0x3e changes.

named_functions.name: queue_one
named_functions.description: Calls queue_command(1, first, 0, 0, 0). finish_node passes the byte at +0x3c.

named_functions.name: pop_record
named_functions.description: Pops the record at 0214b2a8. Its first word becomes the new head. If that word is 0, 0214b2b8 is cleared. An empty list returns 0. The popped record stays in r0.

named_functions.name: send_zero
named_functions.description: Calls send_fifo(7, 0, 0) and repeats while the result is negative. The mailbox word is 7.

named_functions.name: wait_channel
named_functions.description: Calls register_channel(7, on_channel_7), then returns once channel_ready(7, 1) is true. That test is bit 7 of the word at 027fff8c. Until then it calls busy_wait(100) and checks again. return_zero does not take the early exit.

named_functions.name: on_channel_7
named_functions.description: Turns interrupts off, passes its second argument to dispatch_reply, and restores the saved interrupt flag. The first argument is not read.

named_functions.name: count_held
named_functions.description: Returns 256 minus the free-list length from count_free minus the queued-list length from count_queued. A positive result is records on neither list.

named_functions.name: count_queued
named_functions.description: Counts records on the queued list at 0214b2b0. Follows each record's first word. An empty list returns 0.

named_functions.name: count_free
named_functions.description: Counts records on the free list at 0214b2a8. Follows each record's first word. An empty list returns 0.

named_functions.name: count_reached
named_functions.description: Compares the argument with the counter at 0214b2ac. Returns true when the counter has reached that value. A gap of 0x80000000 or more is treated as the counter wrapping past it.

named_functions.name: read_count
named_functions.description: Returns the word at 0214b2ac when the queue head at 0214b2b0 is 0. Otherwise returns the word at 0214b2c8.

named_functions.name: wait_count
named_functions.description: Returns when count_reached says the word at 0214b2ac has reached the saved count. Otherwise reclaims with 0, tries again, calls send_zero, and then reclaims with 1 until the count has been reached.

named_functions.name: file_queue
named_functions.description: Calls clean_lines on 0214b580 for 0x1800 bytes, then send_fifo(7, queue head, 0). A result of 0 or more files the queued list at 0214b2b0 into the next slot of the nine at 0214b2cc and clears 0214b2b0 and 0214b2b4. An empty queue returns 1. A filled-slot count at 0214b2c4 of 8 or more returns 0 when the argument is 0.

named_functions.name: link_record
named_functions.description: Appends a record to the queue. Its first word is set to 0. An empty queue stores it at both 0214b2b0 and 0214b2b4. Otherwise the old newest's first word points at it, and 0214b2b4 moves to it.

named_functions.name: take_record
named_functions.description: Returns a free record. The first call is pop_record. A record from that pop is returned at 020b90c0. An argument of 0 returns 0 when the list is empty. An argument of 1 calls count_held. A positive result loops reclaim_list(0) and tries pop_record again. If that fails, or the count was below 1, it calls file_queue, send_zero, then reclaim_list(1) until a record is available.

named_functions.name: reclaim_list
named_functions.description: Moves one of nine lists at 0214b2cc onto the free list. Argument 0 returns 0 when the word at 0214b2ac matches fresh_word. The index at 0214b2bc then advances and wraps after 8.

named_functions.name: init_queue
named_functions.description: Calls wait_channel, then chains 256 records of 0x18 from 0214b580 onto the free list and clears the queue words. Takes one record, stores 0x19 at +4 and 0214b300 at +8, and files that queue.

named_functions.name: dispatch_reply
named_functions.description: The low byte of the message picks one of eight 12-byte records at 0214cd80. The next byte must match the tag at +8. A matching record with a function at +0 is called with the word at +4. set_reply stores that function and argument.

named_functions.name: set_reply
named_functions.description: Stores a function and an argument into record index × 12 at 0214cd80, adds 1 to the tag byte, and returns the new tag.

named_functions.name: bump_tag
named_functions.description: Adds 1 to the tag byte at +8 of reply record index × 12 at 0214cd80. The add is a byte, so 255 wraps to 0. The new tag is left in r0.

named_functions.name: fresh_word
named_functions.description: Calls invalidate_lines on 0x280 bytes at the block pointed to by 0214cde0, then returns that block's first word.

named_functions.name: second_word
named_functions.description: Same cache drop as fresh_word on the block at 0214cde0, then returns the word at offset 4. step_nodes tests those bits.

named_functions.name: pack_level
named_functions.description: Clamps the argument to -723 through 0. Adds 723 and loads a byte from 0211c950. Returns that byte with a band in the next 8 bits: 3 below -240, 2 below -120, 1 below -60, and 0 from -60 through 0.

named_functions.name: send_fifo
named_functions.description: Writes one word to the send mailbox at 0x04000188. Low 5 bits are the first argument, bit 5 is the third argument, and the rest is the second argument shifted up by 6. Returns 0, or -1 when bit 14 of 0x04000184 is set, or -2 when bit 1 is set.

named_functions.name: channel_ready
named_functions.description: Returns true when bit 1 << channel is set in the word at 027ffc00 + index × 4 + 0x388. Index 0 is 027fff88. Index 1 is 027fff8c.

named_functions.name: register_channel
named_functions.description: Stores the handler at 0214cde8 + channel × 4. A nonzero handler sets 1 << channel in the word at 027fff88. A handler of 0 clears that bit. Interrupts are off for the update.

named_functions.name: result_zero
named_functions.description: Returns 0. It is the entry for argument 8 in the table at 0211cc24.

named_functions.name: build_path
named_functions.description: Entry 5 in the table at 0211cc24. Finds a directory index with step_up and read_name, then writes a path into the buffer at +0x2c. The path starts with 1, 2, or 3 bytes from the parent and the two bytes :/ at 021219d0. Names are copied in from the end, with / between them. A missing index returns 1. A zero buffer at +0x2c returns 0.

named_functions.name: walk_path
named_functions.description: Entry 4 in the table at 0211cc24. Walks the text at +0x38, split on / and \. . is skipped. .. calls step_up when the halfword at +0x20 is nonzero. Each other piece is found with ask_parent(block, 3) and compared by match_name. A piece longer than 127, an empty piece, or a failed read returns 1.

named_functions.name: read_name
named_functions.description: Entry 3 in the table at 0211cc24. Reads one byte through pull_bytes. The low 7 bits are a length at the record's +0x10, and the top bit is stored at +0xc. A length of 0 returns 1. Otherwise the following bytes are read into +0x14 when the block's word at +0x30 is 0, and a 0 byte is stored after them.

named_functions.name: load_block
named_functions.description: Entry 2 in the table at 0211cc24. Copies the three words at +0x2c onto +0x1c. Calls pull_bytes for 8 bytes at parent + 0x28 plus the halfword at +0x30 times 8. Stores the low 12 bits of one returned halfword at +0x28, and returns 0.

named_functions.name: advance_next
named_functions.description: Entry 1 in the table at 0211cc24. Same add as advance_block, then calls the function at the parent's +0x40 with the parent, the word at +0x2c, and the old word at +0x28.

named_functions.name: advance_block
named_functions.description: Entry 0 in that table. Adds the word at +0x34 to the word at +0x28, then calls the function at the parent's +0x3c with the parent, the word at +0x2c, and the old word at +0x28.

named_functions.name: match_name
named_functions.description: Compares two byte strings for the given length. A through Z are folded onto a through z. Returns 0 when every byte matches. A difference returns the gap between the folded bytes. A length of 0 or less returns 0.

named_functions.name: step_up
named_functions.description: Sets bit 2 of the word at +0xc. Stores the parent at +0x2c, 0 at +0x34 and +0x32, and the low halfword of the second argument at +0x30. Then calls ask_parent(block, 2).

named_functions.name: pull_bytes
named_functions.description: Sets bit 9 of the parent's word at +0x10, then calls the function at the parent's +0x44 with the parent, the output buffer, the address, and the count. A result of 0 or 1 clears bit 9. A result of 6 calls yield_heap(parent + 0xc) until bit 9 is clear. The address then increases by the count.

named_functions.name: ask_parent
named_functions.description: Sets bit 9 of the parent's word at +0x10 when bit 2 of the block is set, otherwise bit 8. If bit 1 << argument of the parent's word at +0x4c is clear, the result is 7 and the function at 0211cc24 + argument × 4 is called. Entry 0 of that table is advance_block. Entry 1 is advance_next. Entry 2 is load_block. Entry 3 is read_name. Entry 4 is walk_path. Entry 5 is build_path. Results 0, 1, and 4 are stored at the block's +0x14.

named_functions.name: set_state
named_functions.description: Calls detach_block with the block in r0. Clears the low 4 bits of the word at +0xc, stores the result at +0x14, and calls mark_heaps with block + 0x18.

named_functions.name: start_block
named_functions.description: Stores the second argument at +0x10 and 2 at +0x14, and sets bit 0 of the word at +0xc. An argument from 2 through 8 also sets bit 2. The word at +8 is the parent. Bit 7 of the parent's word at +0x10 returns 0. Otherwise append_block links the block onto parent + 0x14, and the function returns 1 or the result of run_block.

named_functions.name: run_block
named_functions.description: Calls ask_parent with the block and the word at +0x10, then set_state with the block and that result. A nonzero result from scan_parent on the parent calls follow_head with that result. Returns true when the word at +0x14 is 0.

named_functions.name: follow_head
named_functions.description: Sets bit 3 of the block's word at +0xc and calls ask_parent. A result of 6 returns. Otherwise takes the next head from scan_parent on the same parent and repeats. Bit 2 of the block calls mark_heaps and returns.

named_functions.name: scan_parent
named_functions.description: Bit 5 of the word at +0x10 walks the list at +0x18 and calls set_state(node, 3) for each node with bit 1 set. If bit 3 is clear and a head exists, returns that head unless its bit 2 is set, in which case it calls mark_heaps and returns 0. Otherwise returns 0.

named_functions.name: reset_block
named_functions.description: If start_block returns nonzero, stores 0 at +8 and 0xc at +0x10, and clears bits 4 and 5 of the word at +0xc. Returns 1. Otherwise returns 0.

named_functions.name: blank_block
named_functions.description: Stores 0 at +0, +4, +8, +0xc, and the halfword at +0x18. Stores 0xc at +0x10. build_path passes its scratch block.

named_functions.name: append_block
named_functions.description: Unlinks the block from its old neighbors, then links it after the last block reached by following +4 from the second argument. The block's first word becomes that predecessor, and its word at +4 becomes 0.

named_functions.name: detach_block
named_functions.description: If the block's first word is set, that neighbor's word at +4 is set to this block's next pointer. If the next pointer is set, that neighbor's first word is set to this block's previous pointer. Then both of this block's link words are stored as 0.

named_functions.name: register_rom
named_functions.description: Registers the device object at 0214ce94 under the name rom. Opening "/" uses that device.

named_functions.name: restore_divider
named_functions.description: Writes the saved divider and square-root values back to 0x04000280, 0x04000290, 0x04000298, 0x040002b0, and 0x040002b8.

named_functions.name: save_divider
named_functions.description: Copies the hardware divider and square-root unit into the record. save_context calls it with the heap record plus 0x48.

named_functions.name: init_ipc
named_functions.description: Runs once. Calls the IPC handshake thunk, waits until FUN_020b9754(6, 1) returns nonzero, then passes 6 and the function at 020bbe34 to FUN_020b977c.

named_functions.name: send_command
named_functions.description: Saves the interrupt mask, leaves only the IPC-receive bit set, and retries a send until it returns 0. frame calls it as send_command(0xc, 0, 0). The bxeq lr at the end is a normal return.

named_functions.name: read_bits
named_functions.description: Asks channel 8 for a halfword. Writes bit 3 of that halfword to 027c000c and bit 2 to 027c0010. A nonzero result from the read writes nothing.

named_functions.name: on_channel_8
named_functions.description: Handler for channel 8. Returns when its third argument is 0. Otherwise, if a function is stored at 0214cf34, it calls that function and clears the pointer.

named_functions.name: init_channel_8
named_functions.description: Runs once. Clears the two words at 0214cf30, waits for channel 8, registers on_channel_8, clears the first halfword of four 8-byte records at 0214cf54, and copies the word at 027ffc3c to 0214cf2c.

named_functions.name: on_channel_5
named_functions.description: Handler for channel 5. Returns when its third argument is greater than or equal to 0.

named_functions.name: init_channel_5
named_functions.description: Runs once. Clears five words at 0214cf78, waits until bit 5 is set at 027fff8c, and registers on_channel_5 at 0214cdfc.

named_functions.name: on_channel_11
named_functions.description: Handler for channel 11. Returns immediately unless the first argument is 0xb.

named_functions.name: init_messages
named_functions.description: Runs the record setup once, then always registers channel 14. The record is 0214cfc0: three zeros at +0x18, +0x1c, and +0x20, and -1 at +0x24.

named_functions.name: read_card
named_functions.description: Reads bytes off the game card. The rom device uses it to pull a file out of rom.bin.

named_functions.name: on_channel_14
named_functions.description: Handler for channel 14. If the low 6 bits of the message are 0x11, stores 1 at 0214d7e0.

named_functions.name: on_channel_13
named_functions.description: Lasting handler for channel 13. If the low 6 bits of the message are 0x11, calls the function pointer at 0214d7f4.

named_functions.name: ack_channel_13
named_functions.description: Temporary handler for channel 13. If the low 6 bits of the message are 1, stores the halfword 1 at 0214d7e8.

named_functions.name: init_channel_13
named_functions.description: Runs once. Registers ack_channel_13, runs the cartridge setup, then replaces that handler with on_channel_13 and clears 0214d7f4.

named_functions.name: divide_signed
named_functions.description: Divides the first argument by the second. The quotient is the low half of the return and the remainder is the high half. A second argument of 0 returns the first argument and a remainder of 0. The branch at 020c08dc enters an unrolled loop one bit at a time.
